oneTimers: Stock-based compensation and related employer payroll taxes totaled $105.895M in Q1 across cost of revenue and operating expenses — the main reason GAAP shows an operating loss while non-GAAP operating income was $56.001M.
Amortization of acquired intangible assets was $3.241M in Q1 — also excluded from non-GAAP results.
Acquisition-related and other expenses were $0.112M in Q1 — excluded from non-GAAP results.
No one-time compensation charge landed in Q1 2025: the $15.000M one-time compensation charge in the year-ago figures dates to the first quarter of 2024.
otherDetail: Interest income of $21.399M, less $1.443M of interest expense and $3.468M of other expense, net — total non-operating income of $16.488M.

takeaways.text: Revenue hit $479.1M, up 27% YoY from $378.6M a year ago. Cloudflare signed the largest contract in its history — a more than $100M deal driven by its Workers developer platform — plus its longest-term SASE contract to date, and posted the highest year-over-year growth in net new ACV in three years. Remaining performance obligations — work customers have already committed to — stood at $1,864.2M, with 66% expected within 12 months.
takeaways.title: Growth held at 27% with a record deal

takeaways.text: GAAP loss from operations narrowed slightly to $53.2M, or 11.1% of revenue, versus a $54.6M loss a year ago, as operating expenses grew 20% — slower than revenue. But $16.5M of non-operating income, mostly $21.4M of interest income, narrowed the net loss to $38.5M versus $35.5M a year ago. Excluding $105.9M of stock-based compensation and other items, non-GAAP operating income was $56.0M. Free cash flow jumped to $52.9M, 11% of revenue, from $35.6M a year ago.
takeaways.title: A narrower operating loss, still GAAP-unprofitable

takeaways.text: Dollar-based net retention was 111%, meaning existing paying customers spent 11% more than they did a year earlier. Large customers — those paying over $100,000 a year — rose to 3,527 from 2,878, and paying customers overall grew 27% to 250,819.
takeaways.title: Existing customers keep spending more

verdict: Cloudflare grew revenue 27% to $479M and signed the largest contract in its history, but heavy stock-based compensation kept it GAAP-unprofitable with a $38.5M net loss, even as free cash flow jumped to $52.9M.
